chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Oppression is of three types: an oppression that God the Exalted forgives, an oppression that He does not forgive, and an oppression that He does not overlook. As for the oppression that He does not forgive, it is associating partners with God the Exalted. And as for the oppression that God forgives, it is a person's oppression of himself in what is between him and God the Exalted. And as for the oppression that He does not overlook, it is the settling of accounts (debts/rights) among the servants.

key_terms.الْمُدَايَنَةُ: Settling accounts or debts between people

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of oppression in Shia Islam and how does God respond to each?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes oppression into three tiers: major oppression (shirk) which is unforgiven, minor oppression (personal sins between the individual and God) which is forgiven, and social oppression (rights of others) which is not overlooked. This classification underscores the critical Shia emphasis on haqq al-nas (rights of people), noting that while God may forgive personal sins, He does not 'leave' the rights of others until they are settled. The hadith thus bridges theological mercy with social justice, highlighting that divine forgiveness for personal sins does not negate the necessity of settling debts and rights with fellow humans.
